description:
El Salvador’s bereaved mothers unite after gang violence, turning shared grief into solidarity and hope beyond hatred.

El Salvador has long been shaped by cycles of violence, from its brutal civil war to the grip of gangs such as MS-13 and Barrio 18. For many families, losing a child is a harsh reality. Sadness, fear and anger fill their daily lives. Amid this, a group of mothers has chosen a different path. They support one another, share their stories, and work to restore hope. In doing so, they turn personal loss into collective strength and show that courage can exist alongside pain.

Mari has turned her tragedy into a source of resilience, dedicating herself to walking alongside other mothers and offering support in the midst of grief. Beatriz, still searching for her son, finds guidance and comfort in Mari’s presence as she navigates her loss. Mohajerani describes the confrontation as a war in which both sides have struck and been struck. She acknowledges what she calls “painful blows”, including the killing of senior military officials and civilians.

description:
The Qatar government has announced that it is evacuating residents who live in houses close to the US embassy in capital Doha.

“In the framework of maintaining public safety, the Ministry of Interior announces that the relevant authorities are evacuating residents living in the vicinity of the US Embassy as a temporary precautionary measure,” Qatar’s Ministry of Interior said in a statement on X. “Suitable accommodation has been provided for them as part of necessary preventive measures.”

Al Jazeera’s Aksel Zaimovic joins live from Doha.

description:
Voters in Nepal go to the polls on Thursday in an election many believe could see a major political shift. It comes after youth-led protests in September ousted the government. Much of the campaigning has been happening on social media platforms. And established political parties seem to be struggling to adapt.

Al Jaeera’s Tony Cheng reports from Chitwan in southwestern Nepal.

description:
Asia's stock markets tumbled on Wednesday, led by a record drop in South Korea and the biggest sell-off since the pandemic in Thailand. It's all being driven by concern about an oil shock. South Korea's stock market dived more than 12 percent. Fears the Iran war could cripple Asia's fourth-largest economy have sent the country’s currency to a 17-year low.

Al Jazeera’s Jack Barton reports from Seoul.

author: Al Jazeera English
description:
Belgium’s Foreign Minister Maxime Prevot has told Al Jazeera that he “understand[s] why the US and Israel have launched these attacks”.

“Frankly speaking, Iran was not a model student regarding the respect of international law,” he told Al Jazeera from Brussels, citing “threats against its own population”, violence and torture.

“So it was time to say stop to the way Iran was managing the country,” he added.

Still, Prevot emphasised he and other European representatives are advocating for de-escalation and a ceasefire  “as soon as possible”.

European Union foreign ministers are slated to meet their counterparts at the Gulf Cooperation Council tomorrow.

Al jazeera's Usama bin Javad reports
